title: Apportioning Order Reductions to a Missing-Information Correction — Insurance Coverage & Claims Decision Table
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims — corrected claims answering a missing-information denial (CO-16).** The missing-information correction's share of the order's reductions depends on what the remittance did with the rest of the claim.

## Rule

The missing-information correction's share of the order's reductions is:

- the denial's amount divided by **all the denied amounts on the claim**, where the remittance paid at least one line of the claim;
- the denial's amount divided by **the amount the claim billed at filing**, where no line was paid but the plan adjudicated a line to the member or to a contractual adjustment;
- **one**, otherwise, the reductions being taken in full.

## Decision table

| Plan payment line on the claim | Member-responsibility or contractual-adjustment line on the claim | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either | Denial's amount divided by all denied amounts on the claim |
| No | Yes | Denial's amount divided by the amount billed at filing |
| No | No | One |

"All the denied amounts on the claim" means every denial line on the claim, whatever its code, the missing-information denial included.

## Hypothetical example

A claim billed 600.00 USD at filing. Its remittance paid nothing, assigned 50.00 USD to the member, and denied 150.00 USD as CO-16 and 400.00 USD as CO-50. No line was paid but a line was adjudicated to the member, so the share is 150.00 divided by 600.00, that is 0.25.
